back: The whole set of people or items about which information is wanted.
Part of a population, selected so that information about the population can be obtained from it.
A survey that collects data from every member of the population.
Data collected first-hand by the user for a particular purpose (questionnaires, counts, experiments).
Data collected by someone else and reused (published reports, records, newspapers).
Qualitative: categories (colour, language). Quantitative: numbers from counting or measuring.
Discrete: separate values, usually counted. Continuous: any value in a range, measured (height, mass, time).
One stroke per observation; every fifth stroke crosses the previous four to make a gate of 5.
